newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia moves to protect women from sex-slave export.
newsitem.headline: Colombia moves to protect women from sex-slave export.

text.p: The government launched a campaign on Thursday to keep young Colombian women from being duped into "debt-slavery" as prostitutes in Dutch brothels.
Colombian women are routinely lured to Holland via false newspaper ads promising well-paid jobs as models or Spanish- speaking tour guides, a spokeswoman for the Ministry of Justice said.
The women, often poor and undereducated, are then forced into the sex trade to repay cash advances for air tickets, room and board -- which the spokeswoman described as "captivity through debt."
She said the ministry had set up a hot-line for citizens to report cases where they suspected that women were being shipped abroad to work as prostitutes against their will.
At least 30 percent of Holland's prostitutes come from Latin America, mainly from the Dominican Republic and Colombia, the spokeswoman said.
